title: Intra-Fairness Dynamics: The Bias Spillover Effect in Targeted LLM Alignment
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured social biases against individuals from protected classes, including religion. The evaluation was done using multiple-choice questions designed to detect if the model's responses were biased in ambiguous and disambiguous contexts.
findings: Targeted gender alignment generally led to a statistically significant improvement in fairness for the religion attribute across all three models (Mistral 7B, Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen 2.5 7B). Unlike other sensitive attributes such as physical appearance or sexual orientation, religion did not show significant fairness degradation (bias spillover) in ambiguous contexts.
